The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+9$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}=\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+9}+\frac{C}{x-3}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+9)(x-3),$ and we get

$$
{x}^{2}+x+42=(Ax+B)(x-3)+C({x}^{2}+9).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=-2,B=-5,$ and $C=3.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}=-\frac{2x+5}{{x}^{2}+9}+\frac{3}{x-3}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-\frac{2x+5}{{x}^{2}+9}+\frac{3}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use a substitution $u={x}^{2}+9.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+9| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+9).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3}).
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+9)-5\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+3\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+K \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+9)-\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+K\end{aligned}
$$
